notes:
Account summary
- Enterprise insurance carrier evaluating Redwood Dedicated for regulated workloads (customer data, claims docs). Primary motivation: predictable throughput + isolation + “real least-privilege admin controls.”
- Their security team is explicitly asking for: (1) RBAC templates they can adopt without custom policy authoring, (2) SSO/SAML group mapping with clear scoping semantics, and (3) audit logs that are evidence-friendly (SOC2-style) and exportable to SIEM.

Firmographics / org
- HQ: North America (US). Mix of onshore/offshore dev teams.
- Central IAM team owns SSO and group provisioning. Separate Platform Ops team runs internal developer platforms.

Workload / technical requirements
- Initial workload: claims-call summarization + internal adjuster assistant. Inputs include call transcripts + PDF/email attachments.
- Model needs: chat + summarization; some doc-search/RAG (embeddings) likely in phase 2.
- Performance: target P95 < 2.5s for typical 300–800 token generations; stable throughput during business hours (Mon-Fri).
- Reliability: wants clear failover story (region fallback acceptable if within their policy), but prefers pinned model versions for change control.
- Dedicated topology ask: VPC deployment with dedicated GPU pool; prefer us-east; allow burst for end-of-month peak.

Security / compliance requirements (what they repeated on calls)
- SSO/SAML: “No local passwords for admins.” SAML required for Console admin access. Wants SCIM later but not a hard blocker.
- RBAC: separation of duties is a must. They want distinct roles for:
  - Security admin: manage roles/role bindings, audit export, retention settings.
  - Deployment operator: manage dedicated capacity, routing policies, model pinning/rollouts.
  - Read-only auditor: view configs + audit logs, no mutation.
- Permission transparency: they asked for a permission viewer and an explicit permission-to-endpoint mapping (“we need something we can show auditors”).
- Audit logging: export to Splunk (preferred) or QRadar. Needs who/what/when, plus why access was denied (“deny reason”) for admin troubleshooting. Asked if audit logs include the *authorization decision context* (subject, action, resource scope, policy version).
- Retention: asked for configurable audit log retention and controls around export access.
- Key management: prefer KMS integration for secrets at rest; asked about key rotation workflows + who can do them.
- Break-glass: wants documented emergency admin flow with approvals + time bounds + alerting.

- 2025-02-20 (Fireflies: 2025-02-20-security-review-rbac-and-audit-logs): Security review call. Their lead said: “We will not move forward without role templates and auditable enforcement.” Requested sample audit events + SOC2 report.
